bull.b: The Anthropic lease provides unusually long-duration contracted demand and ties future revenue to a major AI customer. This backlog can improve visibility, support infrastructure utilization, and reduce reliance on spot bitcoin economics as HPC capacity is delivered.

HPC leasing is becoming a larger and faster-growing revenue stream, indicating progress in shifting toward contracted data-center infrastructure. Continued capacity additions could make this mix more durable and less dependent on bitcoin prices and mining conditions.

The reported liquidity position gives TeraWulf resources to complete committed projects, support tenant fit-out, and fund near-term expansion without an immediate return to equity markets. That financial runway strengthens execution capacity while contracted sites are built.

bear.b: Recent revenue contraction alongside an extremely negative net margin shows that gross profit is not yet covering the company’s operating and non-operating cost structure. Persistent losses could weaken retained capital and make profitable scaling dependent on successful execution.

The core business has not generated sustainable operating cash, while substantial negative free cash flow reflects heavy investment and ongoing funding needs. Continued cash consumption can constrain flexibility and increase reliance on debt, asset sales, or equity financing.

Very high leverage, thin reported equity, and large interest outflows leave less financial flexibility if projects are delayed or returns take longer to develop. The capital structure can amplify execution risk and divert cash from expansion toward debt service.
